findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category is unset or unmatched
findings.body: The migration unconditionally calls [0]['id'] on the result of joining categories to the embed_category site setting. On installs that never set embed_category, or whose stored value is not exactly a category name, the query returns no rows, [0] is nil, and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration and blocking deployment/upgrades. The fallback on line 15 has the same unsafe [0]['value'] pattern.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are inserted verbatim and can break host matching or the migration
findings.body: Hosts from the old embeddable_hosts setting are interpolated directly into INSERT SQL without normalization or quoting. Values stored as 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' (forms the old setting and specs explicitly allowed) are inserted with scheme/path intact, but EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares them against URI(host).host (a bare hostname), so migrated sites silently lose embedding permission for those hosts. A host containing a single quote also breaks/injects the raw SQL and aborts the migration.

findings.title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
findings.body: The before_validation block calls self.host.sub! without checking for nil. Creating an EmbeddableHost with a missing/blank host (e.g. a direct API POST with no host param reaching the model, or EmbeddableHost.new.valid?) raises NoMethodError instead of failing the format validation and returning a validation error, producing a 500 rather than render_json_error.

findings.title: Update/destroy raise NoMethodError for unknown ids instead of returning 404
findings.body: update and destroy look up the host with where(id: params[:id]).first and immediately call save_host(host)/host.destroy on the result. For a stale or invalid id the lookup returns nil, so save_host dereferences nil.host= and destroy calls nil.destroy, returning a 500. save_host also dereferences params[:embeddable_host] on line 23 without checking presence, so malformed requests crash the same way.

findings.title: Edit action crashes for hosts whose category cannot be resolved
findings.body: The edit action does this.get('host.category.id') unconditionally. A host whose category_id points at a deleted category, the uncategorized sentinel, or a category not present in the client's category list hydrates with category undefined/null (store._lookupSubType returns Discourse.Category.findById(id), which can be undefined), so clicking the pencil throws a TypeError and the row can never be edited or fixed in the UI.

findings.title: Plural _id hydration discards ids and fabricates undefined entries when the collection is not sideloaded
findings.body: For any *_ids key, the new code maps ids through _lookupSubType, assigns the result (which may be an array of undefined when root does not contain the sideloaded collection), and deletes the original *_ids key. Unlike the singular branch, which only replaces the key when a record is found, the plural branch loses the id data and leaves an array of undefined objects for any payload that carries ids without embedding the records, a regression affecting all RestModel types, not just fruits/embeddable hosts.

findings.title: No uniqueness constraint allows ambiguous duplicate hosts
findings.body: Neither the model nor the migration adds a uniqueness validation/index on host. Admins can create two EmbeddableHost rows for the same hostname with different categories; record_for_host then returns whichever row the database happens to return first, so embedded topics from that host are filed into an unpredictable category and host_allowed?/category selection becomes nondeterministic.
